description: Constructed. 'Acute pulmonary emboli in the right lower lobe segmental…' vs 'Chronic pulmonary emboli in the right lower lobe segmental…': diagnosis major (acute vs chronic segmental emboli; acute emboli call for anticoagulation now); 'Solitary 9 mm right lower lobe pulmonary nodule' vs 'Multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules, the largest 9 mm in…': extent major (solitary vs multiple nodules; primary vs metastatic workup); '8 mm ground-glass nodule in the left upper lobe' vs '8 mm solid nodule in the left upper lobe': character major (ground-glass vs solid 8 mm nodule; switches the Fleischner pathway); 'Right upper lobe mass abutting the mediastinal pleura' vs 'Right upper lobe mass invading the mediastinum': extent major (abutment vs invasion of the mediastinum; changes the T stage and resectability); 'Triangular soft tissue in the anterior mediastinum, likely…' vs 'Anterior mediastinal soft-tissue mass, suspicious for…': no error (a status inversion, scored upstream); 'Bilateral ground-glass opacities with interlobular septal…' vs 'Bilateral peripheral ground-glass opacities with…': site minor (both lungs vs peripheral lower-lobe ground glass; a coarser distribution of a diffuse pneumonia, same treatment), character minor (septal thickening vs consolidation within the ground glass; two descriptors of one diffuse pneumonia, same treatment); '4.2 cm lipoma in the left chest wall' vs '3.0 cm left chest wall lipoma': measurement minor (4.2 vs 3.0 cm chest wall lipoma, over 20 %; a lipoma is benign and not followed by its size).
